turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Carla just handed back my shift note on that ruined halibut at table 12 and told me it's way too messy for the closeout packet. Pull up the bistro incident log and tell me what the table actually needs so we can get this fixed.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I checked the incident log. The table records entries across five columns: Date, Incident, Action, Amount, and Approved by. Carla needs the specific incident breakdown, the exact comp action, the dollar amount, and management approval recorded in that structure.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, table 12 was thirty-six dollars comped because the halibut was ruined and remade late, and Carla Vega signed off on it herself. Put that line in and tell me whether it actually covers what Carla wants now, because I can't have this kicked back twice.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Yeah, you're good, I popped that in under a fresh October heading. It's logged as Oct 5, Table 12 ruined halibut entree remade late, Comped entree, 36.00, Carla Vega, so that's every column Carla's table wants and nothing missing on that one. Only thing still hanging on the sheet is that Sep 19 walked tab, 88.20, sitting at Not yet.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Whoa, hold on. Why are you talking to me like we're just messing around in the alley? Carla literally kicked my sheet back because the wording wasn't formal enough for her closeout, and having you talk like that while I'm rushing to fix it is super jarring.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I hear you, and I apologize for how that came across. The row is properly saved in the file, but I understand that tone felt completely out of place.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Look, floor banter is fine when we're running plates or chatting between orders, but this is management paperwork. When we're doing closeout sheets that the GM and the owner audit, breezy chatter just stresses me out. I need to know where things actually stand and what needs to happen next.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: That makes complete sense. Managerial and closeout documentation requires professional clarity and joint coordination rather than casual chatter.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, so from here on out, whenever we're handling manager logs, incident write-ups, or closeout paperwork, speak to me in full sentences without any slang, and always bring up a clear next step so we can decide what to do together.
